suread: review R1 素读（只读 text/，未开 md）

facts.fact: 第二天早晨 Gazzie 在 SUV 旁等她，一句抱怨都没有
facts.anchor: Gazzie met me by her SUV the next morning without a word of complaint

facts.fact: 她以为昨夜那场相处比自己想的更有效
facts.anchor: I assumed our bonding session had a stronger effect than I’d thought

facts.fact: 到场时 Harrison 俯在前台，与 Nova 深谈
facts.anchor: Harrison was leaning over the front desk, deep in conversation with Nova

facts.fact: 两人停下、转身打量她们
facts.anchor: they stopped talking and turned to appraise us

facts.fact: Gazzie 只作职务介绍：Nova 记得 Dart、把两人互相报名
facts.anchor: “Nova, you remember Dart. Harrison, this is Dart. Dart, Harrison.”

facts.fact: 她僵硬地说「我们见过」
facts.anchor: “We’ve met,” I said stiffly

facts.fact: Harrison 补充「只是 briefly」
facts.anchor: “Briefly,” Harrison clarified

facts.fact: Gazzie 宣布：他替她管农场，他说的算
facts.anchor: “He manages the farm for me. What he says goes.”

facts.fact: 她点头装作只是搭车来、不是来打乱现有秩序
facts.anchor: I nodded, like I was just along for the ride, like I wasn’t here to upend the current order of things

facts.fact: Gazzie 看不见时 Harrison 对她冷笑
facts.anchor: Out of Gazzie’s view, Harrison smirked at me

facts.fact: 她有种下沉的预感：他不会让她好过
facts.anchor: I had the sinking suspicion he wouldn’t make this easy

facts.fact: 她没忍住也眯眼回瞪
facts.anchor: Before I could repress the urge, I narrowed my eyes at him

facts.fact: Gazzie 仰头把她的注意力引开
facts.anchor: Gazzie tilted her face toward the ceiling, redirecting my attention

facts.fact: 天花板上一条约十英寸的裂缝
facts.anchor: I followed her line of sight to a crack about ten inches long

facts.fact: 一滴水穿过裂缝落在 Gazzie 脚边、又一滴
facts.anchor: A bead of water dripped through, landing at her feet, then another

facts.fact: 几秒内变成稳定水流，仿佛她的注意让漏势变大
facts.anchor: Within seconds, it was a steady stream, as though her attention had made it worse

facts.fact: Gazzie 骂了一句 Goddammit
facts.anchor: “Goddammit,” she groaned

facts.fact: Harrison 说昨夜雨下得不小
facts.anchor: “Rained pretty heavy last night,” Harrison said

facts.fact: Nova 伸长脖子看，问休息室那道裂是否相关
facts.anchor: “Think the crack in the break room’s related?”

facts.fact: 她判定屋顶漏水是常态问题，就像藻类
facts.anchor: Roof leaks, I decided, must be a recurring problem, like the algae

facts.fact: 办公室并不破败，反而一尘不染、前台与文件柜保养良好
facts.anchor: It wasn’t run-down; it was spotless, the front desk and filing cabinets well-kept

facts.fact: 她觉得自然就是要来搅这处产业
facts.anchor: Nature just seemed intent on interfering with the property.

facts.fact: Gazzie 命令 plumbing 之后叫屋顶工，还在保修期内
facts.anchor: “Call the roofers after the plumbers come by,” Gazzie snapped. “We’re under warranty.”

facts.fact: Harrison 顺口答「On it」
facts.anchor: “On it,” Harrison said smoothly

facts.fact: 她在心里骂马屁精、翻白眼，他抿嘴憋笑
facts.anchor: Suck-up. I rolled my eyes, and he pursed his lips, attempting to hide another smirk.

facts.fact: Gazzie 没察觉两人的交锋，把眼镜推回头发里
facts.anchor: “Good,” Gazzie said, oblivious to our exchange. Pushing her glasses into her hair, she continued.

facts.fact: 她宣布 Dart 自愿把档案数字化
facts.anchor: “In the meantime, Dart has volunteered to digitize our files.”

facts.fact: 她忍不住发出一声抗议的小声音
facts.anchor: Before I could stop myself, I made a little noise of protest.

facts.fact: 昨天 Gazzie 敞开后她本指望能跟着她学农场
facts.anchor: After the way she’d opened up yesterday, I’d hoped she’d let me shadow her, learn more about the farm.

facts.fact: Nova 复述她的想法般反问「Really?」，语气毫无起伏
facts.anchor: “Really?” Nova asked, echoing my thoughts. She spoke without inflection.

facts.fact: 叙述者形容：就算戴安娜王妃幽灵进来要鳄皮礼帽她也这副腔
facts.anchor: I had a feeling she would answer the same way if Princess Diana’s ghost glided through the door and asked for an alligator-skin fedora.

facts.fact: 她忙说本意是给 Gazzie 帮忙，并感激 Nova 替她递话
facts.anchor: “I thought I’d help you, Gazzie,” I added, grateful that Nova had teed me up.

facts.fact: Gazzie：你确实在帮我，是 Harrison 指出档案 neglected 太久
facts.anchor: “You will be helping me. Harrison pointed out we’ve neglected our files long enough.”

facts.fact: 他甜美地笑、头偏一寸；她明白是他出的主意好把她支开
facts.anchor: He smiled sweetly, tilting his head an inch to the side. Of course. He’d suggested a task that would keep me away from her.

facts.fact: Gazzie 命令 Nova 带她过去，随后自己走掉消失
facts.anchor: “Show her,” Gazzie commanded Nova. Then she strode down the hallway and out of sight.

facts.fact: Harrison 最后丢给她一个自得的眼神再跟出去
facts.anchor: Harrison shot me one last smug look before following.

facts.fact: Nova 不慌不忙，从抽屉拿出橄榄绿 macramé 手袋翻找
facts.anchor: Predictably, Nova wasn’t in a hurry. She pulled an olive-green macramé purse from a desk drawer and began to riffle through it.

facts.fact: 她站着挪脚、把表情拧成接近平静的样子
facts.anchor: As I shifted from foot to foot, trying to wrangle my expression into something resembling calm

facts.fact: Nova 掏出润唇膏慢条斯理地涂
facts.anchor: she pulled out a tube of lip balm and applied it leisurely.

facts.fact: 她移开目光研究墙上的 Ida 画像，发丝细节再度吸住她
facts.anchor: Averting my gaze, I studied Ida’s portrait on the wall. Again, her hair’s exquisite detailing drew me in

facts.fact: 每根发丝像一根根画出来的
facts.anchor: each strand seemingly painted one by one

facts.fact: 上次见过之后她唇上的笑似乎更明显了
facts.anchor: Since the last time I’d seen her, the smile on her lips seemed more pronounced.

facts.fact: Nova 保湿完带她走 Gazzie 消失的那条走廊，角斗士凉鞋拖着短毛地毯
facts.anchor: her gladiator sandals dragging on the low-pile carpet

facts.fact: 她礼貌地问 Nova 住附近吗、干多久了；对方单字回答 Yes／No
facts.anchor: I politely asked if she lived nearby, if she’d worked at the farm long. She answered in single-word sentences. Yes. No.

facts.fact: 她判断 Nova 对这家公司不上心
facts.anchor: She wasn’t invested in Greer Fine Alligators, that much was clear.

facts.fact: 她想不通 Gazzie 为何雇她，只当她有她的理由
facts.anchor: I couldn’t imagine why Gazzie had hired her, but I supposed she had her reasons.

facts.fact: 走廊尽头是金属双门，上方又一只摄像头
facts.anchor: The hallway ended in a metal double door. Another security camera hung above it.

facts.fact: 方形窗里透出明亮的白走廊
facts.anchor: A rectangular window revealed a bright white hallway.

facts.fact: 她猜那就是参观时 Gazzie 示意过的加工区
facts.anchor: Presumably, this was the processing area Gazzie had gestured to on our tour.

facts.fact: 一个瘦削、留山羊胡、穿亮绿 T 恤的男人经过窗前：又一个员工
facts.anchor: A thin goateed man in a bright green tee passed by the window. Another employee.

facts.fact: Nova 突然开口：那扇门后一律禁止进入
facts.anchor: “Everything behind that door is off-limits,” Nova said, startling me.

facts.fact: 那扇门锁着，那一侧的其他门也锁
facts.anchor: “It’s locked, as are the other doors to that side of the building.”

facts.fact: 她追问为什么；答：Gazzie 的命令
facts.anchor: “Why?” I asked.

facts.fact: 再问有没有别的原因；Nova 耸肩说危险，还有鳄鱼
facts.anchor: Nova shrugged. “It’s dangerous. Alligators and all.”

facts.fact: 她反问鳄鱼不是被关着吗
facts.anchor: “Aren’t they locked up?”

facts.fact: Nova：过去出过事故
facts.anchor: “There’ve been accidents in the past.”

facts.fact: Nova 不肯多说；她最后看一眼那扇关着的门，退开并自我安慰之后会有正式参观
facts.anchor: After one last glance at the shut doors, I retreated, telling myself Gazzie would give me a proper tour later.

facts.fact: Nova 打开自己身旁那扇门挤进去，她从后面侧身进入
facts.anchor: Opening the door she stood by, Nova squeezed inside. I edged in behind her.

facts.fact: 储藏室从地板堆到近天花板全是档案箱
facts.anchor: It was a storage room filled floor to near-ceiling with filing boxes.

facts.fact: 箱子沤了许多年甚至几十年
facts.anchor: They’d been festering for years, if not decades.

facts.fact: 霉味熏香了空气、让她皱鼻
facts.anchor: Mildew perfumed the air, making my nose wrinkle.

facts.fact: Nova 平板地说这就是档案、以瘫软的手势指箱子
facts.anchor: “These are the files,” Nova droned, ignoring my discomfort as she gestured at the boxes with a limp hand.

facts.fact: 档案只回溯到七十年代
facts.anchor: “They date back to the seventies.”

facts.fact: 她抬高嗓门问生意不是 1800 年代末创立的吗，指望 Gazzie 听见并惊讶于她的知识
facts.anchor: “Wasn’t the business founded in the late 1800s?” I asked, raising my voice in the hopes that Gazzie would hear and be impressed by my trivia knowledge.

facts.fact: Nova：那时法规没那么严、至少佛州不是
facts.anchor: “Regulations weren’t as tight back then. Not in Florida, anyway.

facts.fact: 她追问那不该有更多档案；若始于维多利亚时代该有几间房的材料
facts.anchor: “So shouldn’t there be more files?” If the business had started in the Victorian era, there would be multiple rooms stuffed with papers.

facts.fact: Nova：那时法规没那么严，至少佛州不是；Virginia 在近二十年逼 Gazzie regular 记录文书，是在买下两座分场之时；「她是这么说的」，Nova 那时不在
facts.anchor: Virginia made Gazzie start tracking paperwork regularly in the last two decades, when they acquired the two satellite farms. Or so she said. I wasn’t around then.

facts.fact: Nova 看起来现在也不想在场
facts.anchor: Nova looked like she didn’t want to be around now, either.

facts.fact: 她仰头看高耸的档案箱
facts.anchor: I craned my neck, peering at the filing boxes towering above me.

facts.fact: Nova：缺了这么多仍是量大；可把 2009 年之前的全丢掉，Virginia 说 IRS 大概不会往回查十年
facts.anchor: you can throw out anything dated before 2009. Virginia said the IRS probably wouldn’t dig back more than ten years.

facts.fact: 两人过了一遍扫描流程，听着乏味但不难
facts.anchor: We reviewed the scanning process, which sounded tedious but simple enough.

facts.fact: 结束时 Nova 祝她好运、投来一个同情的眼神
facts.anchor: When we finished, she wished me luck, shooting me a sympathetic glance.

facts.fact: 她脸热：被隔离在空房间配无用档案＝Gazzie 在传话「你不是我们的人」
facts.anchor: By isolating me in an empty room with worthless files, Gazzie was sending a message: You’re not one of us.

facts.fact: 连 Nova 也读出了这层
facts.anchor: Even Nova had picked up on it.

facts.fact: Nova：只是做我的工作；再补一条——别离开这栋楼，你祖母不想有人乱走
facts.anchor: “One more thing: Don’t leave this building. Your grandmother doesn’t want people wandering.”

facts.fact: 她推断几天前那桩未命名的事故发生在外面；她曾听见 Nova 提到 out back
facts.anchor: The unnamed incident from a few days before must have happened outside; I’d overheard Nova mentioning something out back.

facts.fact: 她话没说完就被「公司规定」切断：未经授权的人员不得在行政区外活动
facts.anchor: “Company policy. No unauthorized guests or employees outside administrative areas.”

facts.fact: 她据此断定公司在某种麻烦里
facts.anchor: That settled it; Greer Fine Alligators was in some sort of trouble.

facts.fact: 依据清单：第一次晚餐与办公室里的话、参观时偷听到的急促对话、锁着的门与严规
facts.anchor: Between Gazzie’s comments during our first dinner and in her office, the rushed conversation I overheard on my tour, plus the locked doors and strict rules, it was obvious.

facts.fact: 她想：若证明有用，也许 Gazzie 会告诉她发生了什么
facts.anchor: If I proved my usefulness, maybe Gazzie would tell me what was happening.

facts.fact: 她撬开第一只盖子，霉味变浓
facts.anchor: I cracked open the first lid, and the mildew smell intensified.

facts.fact: 她认命地抽出第一份档案
facts.anchor: Resigned, I pulled out the first file.

relations: Harrison：本章由 Gazzie 亲口定性「替她管农场、他说的算」
He manages the farm for me. What he says goes.
Nova：单字回答、不上心；转述 Virginia 的说法时加「Or so she said」
Or so she said. I wasn’t around then.
无名员工（山羊胡、亮绿 T 恤）：本章新面孔，与 ch08 的 neon-green 衫喂料工是否同一人未写
A thin goateed man in a bright green tee passed by the window.
Ida 画像：本章是办公室墙上那幅的第三次看，笑被认为更明显
the smile on her lips seemed more pronounced
